newsitem.title: FRANCE: French airline flights normal despite strike.
newsitem.headline: French airline flights normal despite strike.

text.p: Air France Europe said flights were operating normally on Monday despite a pilots' strike call over restructuring plans, but unions warned of serious disruption on Tuesday when ground staff join the protest.
"Flights are running normally," a spokeswoman for the state-owned airline said.

Three pilots' and flight crew unions called the 48-hour strike from Monday in a dispute over the unifying of their pay and employment terms with those of parent company Air France in a merger between the two airlines.
The main pilots' union did not back the strike call.
Ground staff unions, whose strike on Saturday forced the airline to cancel all of its flights out of Paris-Orly airport, said they would join the pilots' stoppage from Tuesday at 6 a.m. (0400 GMT).
"Flights could be seriously disrupted," said Leon Cremieux of the Sud-Aerien ground staff union.
Ground staff had staged two two-hour stoppages on Sunday causing only minimal delays.
The airline said management would discuss union demands this week and delay a disputed new working schedule until May 1.
